\chapter{Graph Theory — Reach}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.GraphTheory.Kruskal.Reach
\section{Overview}

This module defines graph reachability over a list of weighted edges $(\mathtt{WEdge}\,n)$
using the reflexive--transitive closure of symmetric adjacency, and establishes its
core structural properties: symmetry, monotonicity under edge-list inclusion, a
cons-decomposition lemma, and lemmas relating total weight to list membership.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Symmetric adjacency]
\lean{Kruskal.SymAdj}
\label{Kruskal.SymAdj}
\leanok
\uses{Kruskal.WEdge}
Given a list of weighted edges $\mathit{edges}$ on $n$ vertices, $\mathtt{SymAdj}\,\mathit{edges}\,u\,v$
holds when there exists an edge $e \in \mathit{edges}$ whose endpoints are $\{u, v\}$
(in either order), i.e.\ $(e.u = u \wedge e.v = v) \vee (e.u = v \wedge e.v = u)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Reachability]
\lean{Kruskal.Reach}
\label{Kruskal.Reach}
\leanok
\uses{Kruskal.SymAdj, Kruskal.WEdge}
$\mathtt{Reach}\,\mathit{edges}$ is the reflexive--transitive closure of
$\mathtt{SymAdj}\,\mathit{edges}$; that is, $\mathtt{Reach}\,\mathit{edges}\,u\,v$
holds when $u$ and $v$ are connected by a path through edges in $\mathit{edges}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Total weight]
\lean{Kruskal.totalWeight}
\label{Kruskal.totalWeight}
\leanok
\uses{Kruskal.WEdge}
The total weight of an edge list is the sum of the weights of all its edges:
$\mathtt{totalWeight}\,\mathit{edges} = \sum_{e \in \mathit{edges}} e.\mathit{weight}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Spanning like]
\lean{Kruskal.SpansLike}
\label{Kruskal.SpansLike}
\leanok
\uses{Kruskal.Reach, Kruskal.WEdge}
$\mathtt{SpansLike}\,F\,E$ holds when the edge list $F$ is at least as connected as $E$:
for every pair of vertices $u, v$, if $u$ and $v$ are reachable in $E$ then they are
also reachable in $F$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Symmetry of symmetric adjacency]
\lean{Kruskal.symAdj_symm}
\label{Kruskal.symAdj_symm}
\leanok
\uses{Kruskal.SymAdj, Kruskal.WEdge}
\difficulty{1}
Fix a list of weighted edges on $n$ vertices, and let $u$ and $v$ be two vertices.
Recall that $u$ and $v$ are symmetrically adjacent when some edge in the list has $\{u,
v\}$ as its pair of endpoints, in either order. If $u$ and $v$ are symmetrically
adjacent, then so are $v$ and $u$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Monotonicity of symmetric adjacency]
\lean{Kruskal.symAdj_mono}
\label{Kruskal.symAdj_mono}
\leanok
\uses{Kruskal.SymAdj, Kruskal.WEdge}
\difficulty{1}
Fix $n \in \bbn$ and two vertices $u, v \in \mathrm{Fin}\,n$, and let $e_1$ and $e_2$ be
lists of weighted edges on $n$ vertices such that every edge of $e_1$ also occurs in
$e_2$. If $u$ and $v$ are symmetrically adjacent in $e_1$ — that is, some edge of $e_1$
has endpoints $\{u,v\}$ in either order — then $u$ and $v$ are symmetrically adjacent in
$e_2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Symmetry of reachability]
\lean{Kruskal.reach_symm}
\label{Kruskal.reach_symm}
\leanok
\uses{Kruskal.Reach, Kruskal.WEdge, Kruskal.symAdj_symm}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\mathit{edges}$ be a list of weighted edges on $n$ vertices, and call two vertices
reachable when they are joined by a path along these edges (in the sense of the
reflexive–transitive closure of symmetric adjacency). Then reachability is symmetric:
for all vertices $u, v$, if $u$ is reachable from $v$, then $v$ is reachable from $u$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Monotonicity of reachability under edge addition]
\lean{Kruskal.reach_mono}
\label{Kruskal.reach_mono}
\leanok
\uses{Kruskal.Reach, Kruskal.WEdge, Kruskal.symAdj_mono}
\difficulty{3}
Fix $n$, let $e_1$ and $e_2$ be lists of weighted edges on the vertex set
$\mathrm{Fin}\,n$, and let $u, v : \mathrm{Fin}\,n$. Suppose $u$ and $v$ are connected
by a path through the edges of $e_1$, and that every edge of $e_1$ also occurs in $e_2$.
Then $u$ and $v$ are connected by a path through the edges of $e_2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Endpoints of a listed edge are reachable]
\lean{Kruskal.reach_of_mem}
\label{Kruskal.reach_of_mem}
\leanok
\uses{Kruskal.Reach, Kruskal.WEdge}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\mathit{edges}$ be a list of weighted edges on $n$ vertices, and let $e$ be a
weighted edge belonging to $\mathit{edges}$. Then the endpoints $u$ and $v$ of $e$
satisfy $\mathtt{Reach}\,\mathit{edges}\,u\,v$; that is, they are connected by a path
through $\mathit{edges}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Lifting reachability along an edge set]
\lean{Kruskal.reach_lift}
\label{Kruskal.reach_lift}
\leanok
\uses{Kruskal.Reach, Kruskal.SymAdj, Kruskal.WEdge, Kruskal.reach_mem_iff}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\mathit{edges}$ and $\mathit{edges}'$ be two lists of weighted edges on $n$
vertices, and suppose that whenever two vertices $a$ and $b$ are symmetrically adjacent
in $\mathit{edges}$ — that is, some edge of $\mathit{edges}$ has endpoints $\{a,b\}$ —
the vertices $a$ and $b$ are connected by a path through $\mathit{edges}'$. Then for any
vertices $u$ and $v$, if $u$ and $v$ are connected by a path through $\mathit{edges}$,
they are also connected by a path through $\mathit{edges}'$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Head–tail decomposition of reachability]
\lean{Kruskal.reach_cons_iff}
\label{Kruskal.reach_cons_iff}
\leanok
\uses{Kruskal.Reach, Kruskal.WEdge, Kruskal.reach_mono, Kruskal.reach_of_mem, Kruskal.reach_symm}
\difficulty{6}
Let $g$ be a weighted edge on $n$ vertices with endpoints $p$ and $q$, let
$\mathit{rest}$ be a list of weighted edges on the same $n$ vertices, and let $a$ and
$b$ be vertices; say two vertices are \emph{$\mathit{rest}$-connected} when they are
joined by a path using only the edges in $\mathit{rest}$. Then $a$ and $b$ are joined by
a path through the edges of the list obtained by prepending $g$ to $\mathit{rest}$ if
and only if at least one of the following holds: $a$ and $b$ are
$\mathit{rest}$-connected; or $a$ is $\mathit{rest}$-connected to $p$ while $q$ is
$\mathit{rest}$-connected to $b$; or $a$ is $\mathit{rest}$-connected to $q$ while $p$
is $\mathit{rest}$-connected to $b$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Reachability depends only on the edge set]
\lean{Kruskal.reach_mem_iff}
\label{Kruskal.reach_mem_iff}
\leanok
\uses{Kruskal.Reach, Kruskal.WEdge, Kruskal.reach_mono}
\difficulty{1}
Fix $n \in \bbn$, and let $l_1$ and $l_2$ be two lists of weighted edges on the vertex
set $\mathrm{Fin}\,n$ that have the same members, i.e.\ $x \in l_1 \Leftrightarrow x \in
l_2$ for every weighted edge $x$. Then for any vertices $a, b \in \mathrm{Fin}\,n$, the
vertex $b$ is reachable from $a$ through the edges of $l_1$ if and only if it is
reachable from $a$ through the edges of $l_2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Total weight of the empty edge list]
\lean{Kruskal.totalWeight_nil}
\label{Kruskal.totalWeight_nil}
\leanok
\uses{Kruskal.WEdge, Kruskal.totalWeight}
\difficulty{1}
Over any number of vertices $n$, the total weight of the empty list of weighted edges is
$0$; that is, the sum of the weights of no edges is $\sum_{e \in [\,]} e.\mathit{weight}
= 0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Total weight after removing an edge]
\lean{Kruskal.totalWeight_erase}
\label{Kruskal.totalWeight_erase}
\leanok
\uses{Kruskal.WEdge, Kruskal.totalWeight}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\mathit{edges}$ be a list of weighted edges over $n$ vertices, and let $e$ be a
weighted edge occurring in $\mathit{edges}$. Then the total weight of $\mathit{edges}$
equals the weight of $e$ plus the total weight of the list obtained by deleting the
first occurrence of $e$ from $\mathit{edges}$.
\end{lemma}
